# OpenAPK.ai

> OpenAPK is an open-source, BYOK, self-hosted workspace for Android reverse engineering. It pairs JADX-based decompilation with an LLM agent that reads decompiled Java, Kotlin, smali, and resources the way a researcher would - file-aware, symbol-aware, package-aware. The agent does the grunt work (identifier recovery, string decoding, crypto reconstruction, call-chain narration, report drafting) while the APK and the analyst's notes never leave the operator's infrastructure.

OpenAPK is licensed AGPL-3.0. There is no SaaS edition; every deployment is a tenant of one. It is the first product in the OpenBin family (https://openbin.ai/), with OpenPE / OpenELF / OpenIPA / OpenWASM planned for other binary formats.

The agent layer supports any of three providers - Anthropic, OpenAI, or AWS Bedrock - with per-user token budgets and a full audit log of every LLM call. Keys are encrypted at rest with a key-encryption key the operator supplies; nothing phones home.

## What OpenAPK does today

- **JADX-powered decompile** - Java + Kotlin extraction with smali, resources, and the manifest one click away. Re-decompile with different options without re-uploading. Full-text search across the tree.
- **Native library analysis** - Ghidra-powered worker decompiles `.so` libraries to pseudo-C with functions, strings, and imports cross-referenced into the project.
- **IDE-style navigation** - go-to-def, find-usages, package-aware breadcrumbs across decompiled source.
- **Identifier recovery** - reads ProGuard-mangled `a/b/c/defpackage` classes in context and proposes meaningful names with reasoning. Renames are word-boundary safe and reversible from the UI.
- **Crypto reconstruction** - static signatures flag `javax.crypto` pipelines, hand-rolled XOR/Base64 obfuscators, and custom decoder shapes. Emits a runnable Python decryptor; when the algorithm maps cleanly, a CyberChef recipe URL.
- **String decoding** - harvests every ciphertext literal that flows into a reconstructed decoder across the project, dedupes, and inlines the decoded output.
- **Grounded source Q&A** - point the agent at any file or symbol. Answers cite file:line. Threaded conversations are persisted per project.
- **Call-chain tracing** - walk methods upward to entry points or downward to leaves, with AI-narrated summaries. Truncation is reported honestly ("8 of 30,000 shown · 29,992 SDK callers hidden").
- **Network call sites** - every HTTP endpoint, header, and request body (Retrofit, OkHttp, HttpURLConnection) cross-referenced to the call site that built them.
- **AndroidManifest entry points** - exported activities, broadcasts, providers; one-click navigation to the handler.
- **Database schemas** - SQLite + Room schema extraction with foreign-key visualization.
- **Evidence capture + reports** - region-grab the screen, annotate (rect/arrow/text/freehand/blur), insert into a report section. MAR (Malware Analysis Report) and VRR (Vulnerability Research Report) templates. Markdown + print-ready PDF export.
- **Community publishing** - published reports are public-readable without authentication; abuse-reportable; author shown as Gravatar identifier, never raw email.

## What OpenAPK is not

- Not a SaaS. The marketing site is at https://openapk.ai/; users run their own instance.
- Not an LLM provider. The operator supplies an API key for Anthropic, OpenAI, or AWS Bedrock.
- Not a sandbox. Static analysis only - no execution, no instrumentation, no emulation.
- Not a JADX or Ghidra replacement. It wraps them and orchestrates an agent on top.

## Key concepts

- **Agent-native**: the UI is built around an LLM agent that reads code and writes reports. Not a chatbot bolted onto a 2008 decompiler.
- **BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)**: every user supplies their own API credentials. The platform never centralizes LLM spend.
- **Self-hosted**: runs in Docker. Air-gap-friendly. No telemetry.
- **Reversible**: renames, decompiles, and report edits are all reversible from the UI. Audit trail per project.

## Glossary

- **MAR**: Malware Analysis Report - section-templated report optimized for malware triage.
- **VRR**: Vulnerability Research Report - section-templated report optimized for vuln research.
- **KEK**: Key Encryption Key - operator-supplied AES-256 master key used to wrap per-user LLM credentials at rest.
- **JADX**: Java decompiler used to extract Android source from APK / DEX. Embedded in OpenAPK; not a separate microservice.
- **Ghidra**: NSA-released reverse-engineering framework, used in a containerized worker microservice to decompile native (.so) libraries.
